interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 12 and an ISUP grade group 5 pathology from the prostatectomy specimen. Driving concerns are the pathological T3a stage with extraprostatic extension noted on the surgical report. Countervailing findings include negative surgical margins, no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no documented lymph node metastasis. A significant discrepancy exists between the biopsy finding (Gleason 0+0) and the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+5). The lack of postoperative PSA data prevents a more refined assessment of current disease status. Future prognosis revision would be significantly aided by obtaining serial postoperative PSA measurements to track trajectory, alongside any available follow-up clinical information. The fixed estimated horizon is 51.41 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 41.13–61.69 months; its coverage has not been validated.
